cases.intent: Empty input returns an empty list.
Repeated separators are allowed, and labels containing only ordinary ASCII whitespace are discarded.
Trim boundaries and collapse a run containing all six ordinary ASCII whitespace characters while lowercasing letters.
A quoted comma is literal, quote delimiters are removed, and adjacent quoted and unquoted text concatenates.
Outside quotes, escaped comma, quote, and backslash are emitted literally without delimiter behavior.
Inside quotes, backslash preserves escaped comma, quote, and backslash literally while the final unescaped quote closes the mode.
Quoted boundary whitespace remains exact and is not removed by trimming ordinary whitespace outside the quote.
Escaped space, tab, and CR are protected at label boundaries and retain their exact characters.
Protected whitespace interrupts ordinary-whitespace runs; each adjacent ordinary run collapses independently to one space.
Ordinary whitespace-only labels disappear, while quoted whitespace-only labels remain nonempty and preserve multiplicity.
Case folding, ordinary whitespace collapse, and quote removal occur before exact deduplication, with first occurrence order retained.
Deduplication compares final strings exactly: two protected-space spellings match, while a collapsed ordinary-space spelling differs.
Empty quoted segments concatenate harmlessly with text, and labels normalizing to empty are discarded.
An escaped quote is literal and does not enter quoted mode, so the following unescaped comma still separates labels.
Lowercase ASCII letters while preserving digits and non-delimiter punctuation exactly.
A trailing unpaired backslash raises ValueError for the whole input even after a valid earlier label.
An unclosed quote raises ValueError for the whole input even after a valid earlier label.
A quote escaped inside quoted mode is literal rather than closing, so reaching end of input still raises ValueError.
A pair of terminal backslashes is a valid escape producing one literal backslash, not an unpaired-backslash error.

rationale: These deterministic ASCII-only cases cover separator scanning, repeated and empty fields, quote toggling and removal, quoted/unquoted concatenation, escaping in both modes, every ordinary whitespace character, trimming and collapse, protected whitespace at boundaries and within runs, ASCII lowercasing, preservation of other literals, empty-label removal, exact stable deduplication, empty input, and both whole-input error classes. Interaction cases distinguish escaped quotes from quote delimiters, protected from ordinary whitespace, and a valid escaped terminal backslash from an invalid unpaired one.
